purpose: Private editorial intake for the Friday Agentic AI governance and operational-risk Top 5. This file is never published directly.

entries.title: Human approval is ineffective unless it is bound to the exact action that executes
entries.summary: The Loopjacking research describes how a human may approve one operation while mutable workflow state allows a materially different operation to execute later.
entries.whyItMatters: Human-in-the-loop checkpoints can appear in a process map without actually constraining the consequential action.
entries.controlImplication: For material agent workflows, bind approved parameters and context to execution through deterministic or tamper-evident controls, then retain evidence of the executed action.

entries.title: Agent loss of control calls for independent scrutiny and defence in depth
entries.summary: Independent analysis of agent boundary failures points to a combination of enabling environment, sufficient capability and misaligned objectives, with lessons from aviation, nuclear power and cybersecurity.
entries.whyItMatters: The operating environment and the independence of the control are as important as the model’s stated objective.
entries.controlImplication: Use layered safeguards, independent evidence sources, incident taxonomy and post-incident learning rather than relying on a single model-based monitor.

entries.title: Proof that an agent remained within its control envelope may become an assurance output
entries.summary: The Proof-of-Control initiative frames auditability as evidence that a particular action remained authorised, rather than a general claim that a governance framework exists.
entries.whyItMatters: Conventional logs and operator attestations may be too weak when agents act at machine speed across systems.
entries.controlImplication: Define a verifiable evidence standard for material agent actions: identity, authorisation, complete action telemetry, integrity of the record and proof of containment where required.

entries.title: Autonomy should be calibrated to impact, reversibility and verifiability
entries.summary: The useful design alternative to binary agent permission is risk-based autonomy, with tighter intervention requirements as actions become harder to reverse or independently verify.
entries.whyItMatters: A valid identity alone cannot show that an agent’s behaviour is safe once it is inside the perimeter.
entries.controlImplication: Set action tiers using business impact, reversibility and independent verifiability; link each tier to permissions, runtime policy enforcement and human-intervention requirements.

entries.title: A minimum agent control plane is converging around inventory, authority, activity and response
entries.summary: Cross-vendor architecture work centres four operational questions: where agents are, what they can do, what they are doing, and how quickly the firm can respond.
entries.whyItMatters: Those questions create a practical minimum standard across agent inventory, identity, delegated authority, observability and containment.
entries.controlImplication: Require every material agent to be a first-class identity with task-scoped access, traceable delegation, runtime monitoring and rapid reversible containment.
